name: Gambia, The
headline: Gambia, The: +5.7% growth in 2025, 7.9% inflation, debt 74% of GDP
sections: Gambia, The is a $2.8 billion economy (2025), the world's 186th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.7% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $3,706 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 1.5% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 7.9% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 11.5% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 10.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 74% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 86% in 2020. The general government balance is −4.7% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −4.1% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 62% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 10.6% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 51% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 66.1 years (2024). Population: 2.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
